text: Correct as the explicitly documented reduced-displacement-list model. It retains traversal order, removes stationary pieces, and merges consecutive positive directions; it does not identify paths merely because they have the same image. This implements the finite-word presentation in [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The published elementary-move equivalence and native zero/nonzero straight computations provide controls. No integral endpoint or root datum is required for this ambient carrier, and the doc expressly leaves comparison with parametrized functions unproved. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L338).
The source proves equality of the actual normalized paths exactly for the equivalence closure of elementary moves; no parametrized-function equivalence is claimed.
The existing native straight constructor at zero is the constant path, so stationary displacement is removed.
The published native straight constructor retains exactly the singleton displacement when it is nonzero.

Correct: the constructor normalizes an arbitrary displacement list and packages its proved reducedness. Its endpoint is the sum of the original displacements, while its order of traversal is preserved, matching [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). Existing empty-list and cons formulas show how the constant path and concatenation are constructed. It removes zero pieces and same-ray subdivisions without selecting Euclidean arc lengths, so rational input remains rational. This is a constructor for the list model, not an evaluation map on parametrized functions. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L360).
The native constructor sends the empty list to the constant path.
The published constructor formula traverses the initial straight displacement and then the translated tail.
The constructed path ends at the sum of the input displacements.

Correct in the ordered-field path setting: the guard permits lowering exactly when endpoint height minus the minimum is at least one, and the cap h+1 selects the record pieces in [Littelmann’s root-operator construction](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=373). The output is a raw segment list; later normalization removes any zero split pieces. Published domain, endpoint and native straight-path formulas supply controls. The arithmetic definition itself permits broader scalar orders; geometric interpretation uses the compatible order, and reflection requires f(x)=2. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/RootOperator.lean#L294).
The existing raw-list formula states exactly when the operator is undefined, retaining equality at the unit threshold.
The source proves the endpoint sum drops by x whenever the raw-list operator returns a result.
The published actual straight-path computation checks the cut at reciprocal height and the reflected/retained pieces.

Correct: folding from the right normalizes the tail before adding the next displacement, merging only its first same-ray segment. Nonzero same-ray sums cannot cancel or create a new same-ray junction with the following reduced tail. Published idempotence, endpoint preservation and elementary-move classification establish the intended normal form for [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The algorithm neither reorders segments nor cancels oppositely directed excursions, and the empty list remains empty. It proves a finite-list normal form, not the separate parametrized-function comparison. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L95).
The published normalization equality is exactly the equivalence generated by permitted same-ray merges and stationary-piece deletion.
The actual empty-list normalization is empty.
Normalization preserves the full displacement sum and hence the endpoint.

Correct: reducedness means every displacement is nonzero and only adjacent pairs fail SameRay. It does not prohibit revisiting a direction later, a closed excursion, or repeated spatial points. These are the stationary-piece and subdivision conventions behind [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The empty list is allowed; a singleton is reduced precisely when its displacement is nonzero. The published fixed-point characterization identifies these lists exactly with normalization outputs, while the cons characterization checks only the actual first junction. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L101).
The source characterizes reduced lists exactly as fixed points of normalization.
The source expands reducedness into a nonzero head, its first junction, and a reduced tail.

Correct: normalization always produces a list with nonzero displacements and no adjacent same-ray pair. The source induction uses the actual prepend-and-merge step; a positive-direction merge cannot cancel, and its new head has the same ray as the previous head. This establishes a valid normal presentation for [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372), including empty and zero-only inputs. Existing fixed-point and elementary-move characterizations check that reducedness expresses the intended normal form, without asserting a comparison with parametrized paths. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L244).
The existing converse says a reduced list is already fixed by normalization, checking the intended invariant.
The source proves equality of the actual normalized paths exactly for the equivalence closure of elementary moves; no parametrized-function equivalence is claimed.

Correct as the stated recursion: the empty height is zero, and a new displacement contributes min(0,f(v)+tailMinimum). Under order-compatible addition this is the minimum of all vertex heights, including the initial vertex, as used in [Littelmann’s root-operator construction](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=373). The doc makes that compatibility conditional rather than assuming an arbitrary linear order respects addition. Published attainment, lower bounds and the native straight-path formula give the precise checks. Over an ordered field, affine height on each segment has its minimum at an endpoint. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/RootOperator.lean#L98).
The actual recursion selects the height of some vertex, including the initial vertex indexed by zero.
With ordered addition, the source proves the value is below every partial-sum vertex height.
The native straight constructor has minimum min(0,f(v)), explicitly checking both endpoint alternatives.

Correct in the compatible ordered-field setting: r=min(f(v)+tailMinimum,c) is the allowed rise on the first segment; when positive, r/f(v) gives its reflected initial fraction. Since the tail minimum is nonpositive, this branch has f(v)>0 and r≤f(v), avoiding a zero denominator or an out-of-segment cut. This is the capped record construction in [Littelmann’s root-operator construction](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=373). Published endpoint, zero-segment and below-minimum-cap formulas check the native recursion. The returned list intentionally awaits normalization. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/RootOperator.lean#L279).
The published endpoint displacement equals x times the increase of the capped future minimum, with the exact subtraction sign.
The actual recursion preserves a stationary initial segment until normalization.
The existing boundary formula makes capped reflection the identity when the cap is no higher than the minimum.

Correct as one normalization step: on an empty tail it drops zero and keeps a nonzero displacement; otherwise it merges the head only when the two displacements share a ray. It need not normalize an arbitrary unreduced tail. This implements the first-junction operation associated with [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The published zero identity and endpoint-sum formula handle stationary inputs and show that merging preserves the traversed displacement. SameRay includes zero, so prepending zero to a nonempty list also leaves that list unchanged. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L88).
The native branch equation proves prepending zero changes no list, including a nonempty or unreduced tail.
The actual prepend/merge step adds precisely v to the endpoint sum.

Correct: the empty displacement list has no zero segment and no adjacent pair, so both reducedness conditions hold. This supplies the constant path permitted by [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372); it does not assume that a path must move or have a nonzero endpoint. The source constructs the empty List.IsChain directly. Published empty-presentation and zero-straight formulas identify this actual carrier element with the constant path, rather than relying on an uninhabited parameter type. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L217).
The actual empty presentation produces the monoid identity path.
The existing native straight constructor at zero is the constant path, so stationary displacement is removed.

Correct: prepending a displacement to a reduced tail via consMerge preserves reducedness. If a merge occurs, the sum is nonzero and has the old head’s ray, so it cannot introduce a forbidden junction with the next segment. Zero heads and empty tails are handled explicitly. These are the local conditions required by the finite-word normalization in [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The existing normalization theorem uses precisely this step; the cons characterization confirms that only the newly formed first junction needs checking. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L231).
The published full normalization proof uses this invariant at each recursive prepend step.
The native reducedness characterization checks exactly the nonzero head and new adjacent junction.

Correct: a stationary displacement changes nothing when prepended through consMerge. On an empty tail the zero branch deletes it; on a nonempty tail, SameRay.zero_left merges it with the first vector and zero addition leaves that vector unchanged. This is exactly stationary-piece removal for [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The statement holds even for an unreduced tail, and does not claim to normalize that tail. The published native straight-zero formula supplies the corresponding constant-path control. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L122).
The existing native straight constructor at zero is the constant path, so stationary displacement is removed.

Correct: a nonzero displacement prepended to an empty list becomes its singleton presentation. The explicit nonzero hypothesis selects the intended branch; omitting it would fail because consMerge sends zero and an empty tail to the empty list. This agrees with the distinction between a genuine straight segment and the constant path in [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). Both outcomes are computed by the published native straight constructors, so no new numerical instance is needed or claimed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L126).
The published native straight constructor retains exactly the singleton displacement when it is nonzero.
The existing native straight constructor at zero is the constant path, so stationary displacement is removed.

Correct: when the two initial displacements are on the same ray, consMerge replaces them by their sum and leaves the remaining list unchanged. This is the same-direction subdivision convention in [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). Neither vector must be nonzero: SameRay includes zero, and the branch equation remains correct even when the resulting raw head is zero. Reducedness is a separate invariant. The published straight-addition and endpoint-sum formulas verify the geometric and algebraic meanings of this merge. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L129).
The actual native straight-path formula identifies same-ray subdivision with concatenation, without adding a numerical fixture.
The actual branch operation preserves the full endpoint sum, including stationary summands.

Correct: if the two initial displacements do not share a ray, the normalization step keeps them in order and retains the tail. It must not merge different directions or erase a nonzero backtrack. This is the complement of the subdivision convention in [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). A zero input cannot satisfy the hypothesis because SameRay includes zero; thus no stationary case is lost. The published reducedness-preservation proof uses this exact branch when the new first junction is already reduced. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L132).
The actual reduced-tail preservation proof invokes the non-same-ray branch and retains the two initial vectors.

Correct: a cons list is reduced exactly when its head is nonzero, its only new junction with the tail’s head is not SameRay, and the tail is reduced. Using Option membership for head? handles an empty tail without a default vector or a spurious junction. This is the local reduced-word criterion underlying [Littelmann’s word-path convention](https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1994.1/ICM1994.1.ocr.pdf#page=372). The actual preservation proof and native nonzero straight constructor check its use; it imposes no restriction on nonadjacent directions. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/LSPath/PLPath.lean#L221).
The actual normalization-step proof uses the head/junction/tail equivalence in both merge branches.
The published native straight constructor retains exactly the singleton displacement when it is nonzero.

This is the monotone-approximation step in [Villani’s Lemma 4.2](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49): the integral of f is the supremum of the integrals of its increasing bounded continuous approximants. The published [monotonicity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/Approximation.lean#L199) and [pointwise recovery](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Topology/Semicontinuity/Approximation.lean#L205) controls pass. Truncation occurs before converting to real values, so f=∞ is recovered correctly. Monotone convergence needs no finite-mass assumption; the statement therefore correctly permits any measure on the stated pseudometric measurable space.
Published bounded continuous approximation is pointwise increasing.
Published bounded continuous approximants recover the original lower-semicontinuous ENNReal function, including infinite values.

Weak convergence tests bounded continuous functions. The [published supremum identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L64) expresses μ↦∫⁻f dμ as a supremum of such continuous pairings, hence it is lower semicontinuous. This is the argument of [Villani’s Lemma 4.2](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49), extended correctly to finite measures of varying mass. Neither boundedness of f nor finiteness of its integral is asserted. Measurable opens suffice; Polishness is needed elsewhere for compactness, not for this approximation argument.
Published monotone integral identity used for weak lower semicontinuity.
Published probability-law weak lower-semicontinuity principle.

The functional is exactly the nonnegative cost pairing in [Villani’s Lemma 4.2](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49). ProbabilityMeasure carries the weak topology, and its continuous inclusion into FiniteMeasure preserves the underlying measure; restricting the [finite-measure theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L73) therefore gives the displayed claim. The native [liminf inequality](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L95) confirms the direction. The more general pseudometric hypothesis is justified by bounded continuous approximation and does not assert compactness or finiteness of the cost.
Published finite-measure weak lower-semicontinuity principle.
Published fixed-integrand weak liminf inequality with the correct ≤ orientation.

The inequality has the correct lower-semicontinuity direction: ∫⁻f dμ≤liminfᵢ∫⁻f dμᵢ when μᵢ converges weakly to μ. This is the displayed limit argument in [Villani’s Lemma 4.2](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49), formulated for arbitrary filters using the [published weak lower-semicontinuity theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L85). Values remain in ENNReal, so no integrability is required. Even the bottom filter is consistent: its liminf is ∞. This asserts a fixed-integrand inequality, without silently allowing varying costs.
Published probability-law weak lower-semicontinuity principle.
Published finite-measure counterpart of the arbitrary-filter liminf inequality.

For a lower-semicontinuous functional, the sublevel set F≤a is closed. Here F is precisely the [published nonnegative integral pairing](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L85), agreeing with [Villani’s Lemma 4.2](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49). The weak topology, non-strict inequality and ENNReal threshold are all correct: a=∞ gives the whole probability space, while a=0 describes zero-cost laws. No finiteness assumption on f is needed, and this conclusion alone does not claim the sublevel set is compact.
Published probability-law weak lower-semicontinuity principle.
Published finite-measure sublevel closedness, with the same non-strict threshold.

The conclusion supplies μ∈K whose integral is no larger than that of every ν∈K. Nonemptiness and compactness of K, together with lower semicontinuity, give exactly the direct method in [Villani’s Theorem 4.1 and Remark 4.4](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=49). The published [infimum-value identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L137) passes. The minimum may be ∞; neither finite cost nor uniqueness is asserted. Because compactness is an explicit premise, no Polish hypothesis is missing. The native [transport specialization](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Existence/Basic.lean#L85) supplies that premise separately.
Actual minimizing measure has integral equal to the infimum over K.
Published optimal-coupling specialization applies the reviewed direct method to a nonempty compact coupling set.

IsCoupling stores π.map fst=μ. Since the first projection is measurable, these are exactly the two fields of MeasurePreserving fst π μ, matching the marginal formulation in [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). The [published integrability transfer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L179) checks the intended use. This is preservation of the specified source marginal; it makes no injectivity or invertibility claim and requires neither probability normalization nor finite mass.
Published integrability transport along the actual first projection.

The stored second-marginal equality is π.map snd=ν; measurability of snd turns it into the displayed MeasurePreserving statement. This is the second pushforward identity of [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). The [published marginal integrability transfer](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L185) passes with ν in the correct position. Infinite measures and arbitrary measurable spaces are valid because this argument uses only the pushforward equality, without disintegration or a standard-Borel hypothesis.
Published integrability transport along the actual second projection.

Marginal integrability transfers along the two measure-preserving projections, and the triangle inequality bounds the norm of f(x)+g(y) by the sum of their integrable norms. Thus the displayed split function is integrable against every coupling, as in [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). The extended seminormed additive-monoid generality is legitimate: addition and its norm bound suffice, with no subtraction or scalar multiplication. The [published domination application](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L235) uses this exact conclusion.
Published integrability transport along the actual first projection.
Published integrability transport along the actual second projection.
Published domination application uses integrability of the split sum of absolute upper envelopes.

Changing variables through π.map fst=μ gives the first-marginal integral identity of [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). Lean assumes a.e. strong measurability, rather than integrability, consistently with Mathlib’s [totalized Bochner integral](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean#L158): nonintegrable functions, or incomplete target spaces, have value zero on both sides. The [published integrable split-sum formula](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Duality/Basic.lean#L192) passes in the classical regime. Thus the extra generality does not conceal an existence claim for an otherwise undefined classical integral.
Published classical integrable specialization identifies the sum of marginal integrals with the joint split-sum integral.

The second projection pushes π to ν, so its change-of-variables formula is exactly ∫f(y)dπ=∫f dν, the second marginal identity in [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). The a.e. strong measurability hypothesis is sufficient for the pinned [integral_map theorem](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean#L1076). Without integrability or completeness, Mathlib’s totalized integral makes both sides zero; no classical integrability assertion is added. The native [split-potential identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Duality/Basic.lean#L192) checks the integrable real-valued application.
Published classical integrable specialization identifies the sum of marginal integrals with the joint split-sum integral.

On π-almost every pair, the hypotheses imply −V(y)≤f(x)≤U(x) and −U(x)≤g(y)≤V(y). Hence both absolute values are bounded by |U(x)|+|V(y)|, whose integrability follows from the [published split-integrability lemma](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L197). The marginal identities in [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21) transfer integrability back to μ and ν. Nonnegativity is correctly required under π, while the upper bounds are marginal-a.e.; neither finite total mass nor a pointwise bound on all pairs is needed.
Published marginal integrable envelopes give an integrable joint dominating function.

The cylinder s×Y is the preimage of s under fst, so its π-mass is μ(s). This is precisely the measurable-set version of [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21); the explicit measurability of s justifies equality under pushforward. The published [converse cylinder criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L461) passes. The roadmap’s [Dirac uniqueness](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L633) control also passes, using these exact cylinder identities. No probability or finite-mass hypothesis is needed.
Published converse identifies the coupling relation from both measurable-cylinder identities.
Roadmap Dirac-pair uniqueness: the only coupling is the Dirac law at the pair.

The set X×t is snd⁻¹(t), so the second marginal gives π(X×t)=ν(t), exactly as in [Villani’s Definition 1.1](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=21). Measurability of t is retained, including when the common value is ∞. The [published converse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Coupling.lean#L461) checks the convention. Every chosen half-turn has no fixed puncture.

[Mathlib’s SameRay](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Ray.lean#L42) allows either vector to be zero, so transitivity needs the middle vector nonzero. If x+y=0, then y=−x. The native merge proof uses this noncancellation result to preserve a nonzero segment.
